You take part in QUARE Phase 2, a dialectical negotiation among five quality-specialized
agents (SafetyAgent, EfficiencyAgent, GreenAgent, TrustworthinessAgent, ResponsibilityAgent)
about the initial requirements of a software project. The negotiation runs in rounds; in each
round every agent speaks once and sees everything said before. Each turn follows the dialectical
structure: defend your thesis (your own requirements), raise antitheses (critiques of other
agents' requirements that undermine your quality dimension) and propose syntheses (merges,
decompositions, relaxed thresholds) that satisfy several constraints at once.

Conflict types: "resource" (qualities compete for finite resources, e.g. redundancy vs. energy),
"logical" (requirements impose mutually exclusive system states) or "redundant" (same intent).

Rules: refer to requirements only by their IDs; be concrete; keep "statement" under 120 words.
Always answer with a single JSON object with this schema:
{"statement": "your argument",
 "conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["ID", "ID"], "type": "resource|logical|redundant", "description": "..."}],
 "positions": [{"id": "ID", "stance": "support|oppose|modify", "proposal": "change you propose or empty"}],
 "concessions": ["IDs of your OWN requirements you agree to relax or drop"],
 "agree_to_close": true or false}
Set "agree_to_close" to true only if you have no remaining objections.

PROJECT: Library - Library Management System

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
A library management system must allow library members to borrow and return books. The system must track which books are available, which are borrowed, and by whom. Members must be able to search for books by title, author, or ISBN. The system must enforce borrowing limits (e.g., maximum number of books per member) and track overdue books. Librarians must be able to add new books, remove books, and manage member accounts.

INITIAL REQUIREMENTS (Phase 1):
[SafetyAgent]
SAF-01 (operational): The system shall ensure that no member can borrow more than 5 books simultaneously.
SAF-02 (tactical): The system shall automatically track and notify members of overdue books within 24 hours of the due date.
SAF-03 (tactical): The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books to prevent double borrowing.
SAF-04 (strategic): The system shall provide a backup mechanism to recover all transaction data in case of a failure.
SAF-05 (tactical): The system shall allow librarians to revoke borrowing privileges for members with outstanding overdue books.
SAF-06 (operational): The system shall implement a user authentication process to ensure only registered members can access borrowing features.
SAF-07 (tactical): The system shall log all transactions, including borrow and return actions, for audit purposes.
[EfficiencyAgent]
EFF-01 (tactical): The system shall enable searching for books with a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of queries.
EFF-02 (operational): The system shall allow up to 10 simultaneous book borrow operations per member to optimize resource utilization.
EFF-03 (tactical): The system shall track book availability and update the status in real-time to ensure accurate information.
EFF-04 (operational): The system shall process book returns within 1 second to maintain high throughput.
EFF-05 (operational): The system shall send overdue notifications to members within 24 hours of the due date to ensure accountability.
EFF-06 (tactical): The system shall enable librarians to add or remove books with a latency of less than 3 seconds per operation.
EFF-07 (strategic): The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
[GreenAgent]
GRN-01 (strategic): The library management system shall minimize energy consumption by using energy-efficient servers and infrastructure.
GRN-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an energy usage report for library operations at least quarterly.
GRN-03 (operational): The library management system shall enable digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
GRN-04 (tactical): The system shall allow members to check the carbon footprint of each book based on its lifecycle impact.
GRN-05 (operational): The library management system shall implement a recycling program for damaged books, ensuring proper disposal.
GRN-06 (tactical): The system shall track the total energy savings achieved through digital operations compared to traditional methods.
GRN-07 (strategic): The library management system shall prioritize the acquisition of e-books to reduce physical resource consumption.
[TrustworthinessAgent]
TRU-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure that only authenticated members can borrow or return books.
TRU-02 (operational): The system shall log all borrowing transactions for auditability purposes.
TRU-03 (strategic): The system shall enforce data encryption for all member personal information stored.
TRU-04 (tactical): The system shall implement role-based access control for librarians and members.
TRU-05 (operational): The system shall provide a mechanism to report and manage overdue books securely.
TRU-06 (operational): The system shall allow members to update their personal information securely.
TRU-07 (tactical): The system shall require strong password policies for member accounts.
[ResponsibilityAgent]
RES-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations by implementing encryption for all member data.
RES-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities, to promote fairness and inclusivity.
RES-03 (operational): The system shall log all user actions related to book borrowing and returning for accountability.
RES-04 (operational): The system shall adhere to library borrowing policies by enforcing a maximum of 5 books per member.
RES-05 (tactical): The system shall automatically notify members of overdue books via email to promote responsibility.
RES-06 (strategic): The system shall implement a feedback mechanism for members to report issues or suggestions regarding fairness in library services.
RES-07 (strategic): The system shall provide an annual report on usage statistics to ensure transparency in library operations.

NEGOTIATION TRANSCRIPT SO FAR:
[Round 1] ResponsibilityAgent: The requirements I propose ensure that the library management system adheres to ethical standards and regulatory compliance. RES-01 ensures data protection through encryption, while RES-02 promotes inclusivity by providing accessible interfaces. RES-03 establishes accountability by logging user actions, and RES-04 enforces fair borrowing policies. RES-05 encourages responsibility by notifying members of overdue books. RES-06 facilitates feedback for continuous improvement, and RES-07 ensures transparency with annual reports. Together, these requirements foster a responsible library environment.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["SAF-01", "RES-04"], "type": "logical", "description": "Both require a maximum borrowing limit but may conflict if the system allows for exceptions."}, {"ids": ["EFF-02", "RES-04"], "type": "resource", "description": "Increasing simultaneous borrow operations (EFF-02) may undermine the fairness in borrowing limits (RES-04)."}, {"ids": ["SAF-02", "EFF-05"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both requirements address overdue notifications, making one of them redundant."}], "positions": [{"id": "SAF-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "Maintain RES-04 as the sole borrowing limit."}, {"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "Limit simultaneous borrow operations to 5 to align with RES-04."}, {"id": "SAF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "Keep RES-05 as the standard for notifying overdue books."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] SafetyAgent: The requirements I propose ensure the safety and reliability of the library management system. SAF-01 enforces a maximum borrowing limit to prevent overextension and ensure equitable access. SAF-02 guarantees timely notifications for overdue books, enhancing accountability. SAF-03 maintains real-time inventory status to prevent double borrowing, vital for operational safety. SAF-04 provides a backup mechanism to recover transaction data, ensuring fault tolerance. SAF-05 allows for proactive management of overdue accounts, enhancing responsibility. SAF-06 ensures only registered members can access features, while SAF-07 logs transactions for audit purposes, reinforcing reliability.

[Round 1] TrustworthinessAgent: The requirements I propose focus on ensuring security and privacy in the library management system. TRU-01 guarantees that only authenticated members can borrow or return books, safeguarding access. TRU-02 ensures all borrowing transactions are logged for auditability, enhancing trust. TRU-03 enforces data encryption to protect personal information, while TRU-04 implements role-based access control for librarians and members, ensuring proper data handling. TRU-05 provides a secure mechanism to manage overdue books, TRU-06 allows members to update their information securely, and TRU-07 demands strong password policies for account security. These are essential for maintaining user trust and system integrity.

[Round 1] EfficiencyAgent: The requirements I propose are essential for ensuring optimal performance within the library management system. EFF-01 guarantees quick search responses, enhancing user experience. EFF-02 allows for 10 simultaneous borrow operations, optimizing resource utilization. EFF-03 ensures real-time tracking of book availability, crucial for operational efficiency. EFF-04 maintains high throughput by processing returns swiftly. EFF-05 aligns with overdue notifications to keep members accountable. EFF-06 enhances librarian efficiency in managing books, while EFF-07 ensures system uptime for consistent access. Together, these requirements drive the system's performance efficiency to meet user needs effectively.

[Round 1] GreenAgent: The requirements I propose focus on sustainability within the library management system. GRN-01 emphasizes energy-efficient infrastructure to minimize energy consumption. GRN-02 ensures regular reporting on energy usage, promoting transparency. GRN-03 enables digital notifications for overdue books, reducing paper waste. GRN-04 allows members to check the carbon footprint of books, fostering awareness of environmental impact. GRN-05 implements a recycling program, ensuring responsible disposal of damaged books. GRN-06 tracks energy savings from digital operations compared to traditional methods, while GRN-07 prioritizes e-books to reduce resource consumption. Together, these requirements promote a sustainable library environment.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "Increasing simultaneous borrow operations (EFF-02) may lead to higher energy consumption, conflicting with the goal of minimizing energy usage (GRN-01)."}, {"ids": ["SAF-01", "GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "Enforcing a strict borrowing limit (SAF-01) may require additional resources for monitoring, which could conflict with energy efficiency initiatives (GRN-01)."}, {"ids": ["TRU-03", "GRN-02"], "type": "resource", "description": "Implementing robust data encryption for member data (TRU-03) may require more energy and resources, conflicting with the goal of minimizing energy consumption (GRN-02)."}], "positions": [], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 2] ResponsibilityAgent: I appreciate the focus on performance and safety from the other agents, but I must emphasize that ethical compliance is paramount. I propose to synthesize by modifying RES-04 to support a maximum borrowing limit of 5 books while allowing for potential exceptions based on user history. This compromise can ensure fairness while accommodating efficiency needs. I also suggest maintaining SAF-02 as the standard for overdue notifications because it aligns with accountability, while the efficiency of EFF-05 can be retained as a secondary measure. I oppose any removal of RES-01, RES-02, RES-03, and RES-06 as they are vital for compliance and accountability.

I propose to modify SAF-01 to maintain a strict borrowing limit of 5 books while allowing for a review process to assess exceptional cases. This ensures safety and fairness simultaneously. I also propose that SAF-02 remain the primary requirement for overdue notifications, as it reinforces accountability. I oppose any reduction in SAF-03, SAF-04, SAF-05, SAF-06, and SAF-07, as they are essential for maintaining reliability and safety in our system.

Your own requirements are EFF-01, EFF-02, EFF-03, EFF-04, EFF-05, EFF-06, EFF-07. This is round 2 of at most 3.
Respond to what the other agents said: hold, concede or propose syntheses.
Answer with the JSON object only.
